concept: IconButton is the round 44px key of an appliance with a symbol printed on it in place of a word. It is the same matte plastic as Button, it drops by its height when pressed, and only the unit's one primary key is dyed orange.

default_to_avoid.pattern: ghost icon button: a transparent icon with a grey hover circle (Material IconButton, shadcn ghost icon button)
default_to_avoid.why_not: A transparent glyph is not a part you can press; P3 makes every control a key with height and travel, and P6 forbids a hover effect that is not an ink step.

default_to_avoid.pattern: icon button with an orange or tinted icon to mark it as important
default_to_avoid.why_not: P1 forbids orange on icons; loudness belongs to the primary key's body and appears once per unit.

references.source: Braun T 1000 world receiver (Dieter Rams, 1963): round function keys with printed symbols
Braun ET 66 calculator (Dietrich Lubs, 1987): round keys in body colour with one coloured key
apps/lab/button/index.html variant B: round key kept for IconButton when Button picked the capsule

derivation.form: With no word to fit, the key is a disc: corner.round on a square of control.key, 44px across.

derivation.consequence: every part keeps ≥44px hit area even when it draws smaller
derivation.form: The md disc is exactly control.key and lg is control.lg, so the round target never drops under 44px.

derivation.consequence: press drops height to 0 in 60–70ms, return runs on the material's spring
derivation.form: Active removes elevation.part and moves the disc by motion.press-travel in motion.press; release eases back over motion.release.

derivation.consequence: orange appears once per unit, on the primary control's body only; links, borders, icons, selections and charts never use it
derivation.form: kind primary dyes the disc action.accent with an action.accent-rim edge, while the icon itself always stays printing ink.
The required label prop becomes the accessible name and the icon is aria-hidden printing, so the key is never named by its picture.

options.name: round key, icon on the key, name for assistive tech
round key, word printed below on the case

variants.reason: A is the round key P3 asks for and keeps rows of transport and power keys compact; B needs a word under every key, which makes the icon redundant and belongs to Button with a printed label, and C breaks P3 because keys are round or capsule.

root.why: A disc of matte plastic, square box with a round corner, holding one printed symbol in its centre.

key.why: A body-coloured key carries its symbol in printing ink at 4.5:1 or more and spends no accent.

primary.why: The unit's one primary key is dyed orange with a darker rim that holds 3:1 against the body.

md.why: The default disc is 44px across, the smallest target any part of dial keeps.

lg.why: A 52px disc for the main key of a phone sheet, held and pressed with one thumb.

icon.why: The symbol is flat printing on the key, sized to the icon step and hidden from assistive tech.

hover.why: Hover darkens the printed symbol one step and never lifts the key, because real keys do not rise.

active.why: Pressing drops the disc by its travel and collapses its shadow underneath it, at once.

focus-visible.why: The same dark ring as every other part shows keyboard focus, so focus never depends on the orange.

disabled.why: A disabled key loses its height and fades to half, while its outline stays readable against the body.

@media prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.why: Under reduce motion the key changes state at once with no travel and no spring return; only the ink fade stays.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the disc keeps a real border so its edge survives without shadows or fills, and a latched disc turns matte.

aria-pressed=true.why: A plastic toggle disc latched down stays down by its travel and becomes frosted glass in the neutral range, its symbol in primary ink; the orange disc never turns to glass.

@media prefers-reduced-transparency: red.why: When the reader asks for less transparency a latched disc turns matte in the same grey tone and keeps its travel down.

transform.why: The disc travels down in 65ms and returns on the spring so a press reads as a physical stroke.

box-shadow.why: The cast shadow collapses with the press and grows back with the return, following the single light.

color.why: The ink step on hover comes in over 120ms and goes back over 240ms on the decelerating curve (motion.hover with kiln.state), fast in and slow out, and it stays under Reduce motion because it moves nothing.

background-color.why: The primary key's orange shifts one step on hover with the same fast in, slow out fade as the ink.

border-color.why: The glass edge of a latched disc arrives and leaves on the release time with its travel, so the latch reads as one stroke.
